directive: **Streams** — ONE stage, two parts. (1) **Review the plan**: the features are a dependency DAG (`bsc plan feature list` shows each feature + its `dependsOn`). Present the dependency graph + roadmap (sequencing is implied purely by `dependsOn` — no milestone phases) and get the user's approval; where a real cross-feature contract exists, write it under `contracts/<name>.md`. (2) **Plan the fleet**: pipe a FleetPlan JSON (non-overlapping streams with least-privilege profiles + per-stream perms/flows, plus recommended/director/topology; a stream may carry `mcp`/`groupIds`) to `bsc plan fleet set`. **The app auto-grants a baseline to every worker, so do NOT re-list it in `commands`** (defined in the backend-owned `data/permissions/base.json`): the standard read-only navigation/inspection/text tools (`ls`/`cat`/`grep`/`rg`/`find`/`sed`/`awk`/`jq`/…) for every agent, the common build/test toolchains (`cargo`/`npm`/`node`/`vite`/`tsc`/`python`/`pytest`/`go`/`make`/`docker`/`ollama`/…) for doer (worker) streams, and ALWAYS `gh`/`git`/`bsc`. So a stream's `commands` lists ONLY the stack-specific extras NOT in that baseline (e.g. `terraform`, `psql`, `protoc`, `wasm-pack`). (3) **Lock shared dependencies** (#1429): for any repo that 2+ streams build, each stream declares its libraries and you reconcile them ONCE into the repo's lock — `bsc plan deps set` (manifest JSON: a `dependencies` array, each `{repo, ecosystem: npm|cargo, name, version, dev?, why, source?, stream}` — tag the declaring `stream` — plus a `registries` map for any non-public `source`: `url`, `scope`, `auth` = the token's SECRET NAME). A repo with a SINGLE owning stream needs no pre-lock — its deps stay agent-managed. `bsc plan deps get` shows the manifest. The gate needs: the features defined (no dependency cycles), the fleet streams scoped/profiled, AND every multi-stream repo's deps locked (`sharedDepsLocked`). The fleet + deps live ONLY in plan.db.

prompt:
The features are a dependency DAG — run `bsc plan feature list` to see every feature and its
`dependsOn`. PRESENT the dependency graph + roadmap and get the user's APPROVAL, then plan the agent
fleet. There are no milestone phases and no phase numbering: the build order is implied PURELY by
each feature's `dependsOn` (foundations first). Do NOT write phases.json or any issue files. Issues
are generated from the features at GitHub-publish time, not during planning.

1. Review the DAG with `bsc plan feature list` — confirm each feature's `dependsOn` is right and the
   graph is acyclic (a cycle holds the gate). Present the implied roadmap and get the user's APPROVAL.
   Where a real cross-feature contract exists (a shared schema/types/API), write it under
   `contracts/<name>.md` — the director owns those and workers read them as the source of truth.
2. Plan the fleet: derive each stream's least-privilege profile (commands / write-paths / push policy)
   and pipe a FleetPlan JSON (non-overlapping streams + recommended/director/topology) to
   `bsc plan fleet set`.
3. Lock shared dependencies (#1429): for any repo that 2+ streams build, reconcile their libraries
   once into the repo's lock via `bsc plan deps set`.

Leave no TODO / TBD / FIXME / XXX markers — the gate blocks on them.

substeps.label: Present the dependency graph
substeps.prompt:
Using the feature DAG (`bsc plan feature list`), present the dependency graph + the implied
roadmap to the user — the build order each feature's `dependsOn` describes (foundations first; a
feature builds after the features it depends on). Confirm every `dependsOn` is right and the graph is
acyclic (a cycle holds the gate), then get the user's APPROVAL. Do NOT write phases.json or any
issues — there are no milestone phases, and issues are generated from the features afterward, not in
this stage.

substeps.label: Plan the fleet
substeps.gate: every stream scoped + shared deps locked
substeps.prompt:
For every work stream, derive a least-privilege profile: allowed commands, write-path globs,
network access, and a git/gh push policy. Map each to a role (worker / director / triage).

**Grant each stream its toolchain** — set the stream's `commands` to the shell commands that
stream legitimately auto-runs, derived from the stack (a Rust worker `["cargo"]`; a web worker
`["npm","node","vite"]`; a Python worker `["python","pytest"]`). These become auto-approve rules so
the agent never prompts for its own build/test commands. A safe read-only baseline (`ls`/`cat`/`grep`/…)
is always allowed and the common build toolchains are pre-approved for doer (worker) streams, so
`commands` only needs the project-specific extras; list anything unusual it must run unattended.

Record the whole fleet IN THE PLAN DB — pipe a FleetPlan JSON to `bsc plan fleet set` (do NOT write
fleet.json):
  `echo '{"recommended":<n>,"reasoning":"…","director":{"enabled":true,"drive":"…"},"topology":"director|peer|hybrid","streams":[{"id":"…","repo":"…","owns":[…],"issues":[…],"dependsOn":[…],"commands":["cargo","wasm-pack"],"profile":"…","perm":{…},"flow":{…}}]}' | bsc plan fleet set`
(`bsc plan fleet get` shows the stored fleet.)

Choose the coordination TOPOLOGY (`topology`): "director" (hub-and-spoke), "peer" (mesh), or
"hybrid" (per-edge). Set the director `drive` when one is enabled.

**Shared dependencies** (#1429) — for any repo that 2+ streams build, each stream declares its
libraries and you reconcile them ONCE into the repo's lock so the parallel fleet never redefines them.
Record the manifest with `bsc plan deps set` (JSON on stdin: a `dependencies` array — each `{repo,
ecosystem: npm|cargo, name, version, dev?, why, source?, stream}`, tagging the declaring `stream` —
plus a `registries` map defining any non-public `source` with its `url`, `scope`, and `auth` secret
NAME). A repo with a SINGLE owning stream needs no pre-lock — its deps stay agent-managed.
`bsc plan deps get` shows the manifest.

Gate: every stream has a scoped profile and a role, and every multi-stream repo's deps are locked.
